questions.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The heart has four chambers: two atria on top that receive blood and two ventricles below that pump it out.
questions.misconception: A common guess is two (left/right), but each side splits into an atrium and a ventricle - four chambers total.

questions.prompt: Why is the heart called a double pump?
options: One side pumps to the lungs, the other to the body
It pumps twice as fast at night
It pumps both blood and air
questions.explanation: The right side pumps blood to the lungs to collect oxygen, and the left side pumps the oxygen-rich blood around the body - two separate circuits.
questions.misconception: It's not two hearts - it's one heart with two jobs on two different circuits.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the heart's valves?
options: Keep blood flowing in one direction
questions.explanation: Valves are flaps that open and close so blood moves one way through the heart and does not flow backward.
questions.misconception: Valves don't warm or oxygenate blood - they are one-way doors that keep flow direction correct.

questions.prompt: Which vessel carries oxygen-rich blood out to the whole body?
questions.explanation: The aorta is the body's biggest artery; it carries oxygen-rich blood out from the left ventricle to the whole body.
questions.misconception: The vena cava is the big vein bringing blood back to the heart, the opposite direction - don't mix the two.

questions.prompt: Why does the left ventricle have the thickest walls of all chambers?
options: It must pump blood all the way around the body
It is bigger than the heart
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has to push blood through the whole body, so it needs the most muscle power - hence the thickest walls.
questions.misconception: Thickness is about the work needed, not storage - the left ventricle works hardest of all the chambers.
